text:
nina: Quick summary from HeliosMetrics POC run — ran a focused throughput+latency sweep to validate interactive SLA. dropping config, topline, and recommended mitigations.

cal: nice, paste the harness + headline numbers so I can draft the quote.

nina: test config: model=redwood-13b-4k-quant, infra=dedicated-1xH100 + spare burst slot, concurrency target=110, batch_target=10, kv_cache=enabled, prefix_cache=off (baseline). runner=k6 + small go client to emulate agent mix. traffic mix: 80% chat (avg out=140 tokens), 20% embeddings. arrival pattern: steady poisson 90 qps, short microbursts to 200 qps for 25s every 12m.

mike-eng: reminder: Helios asked for interactive p95 <350ms for chat. Did we hit that?

nina: baseline 40m soak results:
- sustained throughput: 90 qps stable
- chat p50 end-to-end: 210ms
- chat p95 end-to-end: 680ms
- embeddings p95: 150ms
- error rate during bursts: 3.1% (timeouts/retries)
- observed GPU util: 66% avg, mem headroom ~11GB
- hosted-equivalent cost estimate: ~$0.48 / 1k chat tokens (rough)

cal: 680ms p95 is well above 350ms. root causes?

nina: quick analysis: ingress queueing during bursts, several long-tail kernel stalls on 1 worker traced to a slow attention kernel on some sequences, and prefix cache cold misses for variant prompts.

sophie: what are low-effort mitigations we can offer in the proposal? We need an option we can commit to quickly.

nina: low-effort: 1) enable prefix prewarm for top-120 prompts, 2) reduce batch_target to 8 during burst windows, 3) add an autoscale burst worker policy (+1 worker for short windows). ops-bot created the suggestion for the last one.

ops-bot: [automated] autoscale suggestion created: RB-7102 by nina. policy: +1 worker when 1m avg qps >150, cooldown 3m. link: https://console.redwood.example/rb/7102

mike-eng: medium-effort if low-effort doesn't reach 350ms?

nina: medium-effort: eng-runtime to investigate and patch the attention kernel path for the nasty sequence pattern — estimate 2-3 days. Could be optional paid work in the SOW.

cal: go ahead and run the primed + batch=8 experiment. capture CSV + flame graphs. We present priming + burst buffer as baseline; runtime tuning as optional add-on.

nina: running now. k6 snippet we used for chat runner: 
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-13b-4k-quant', prompt: 'Short answer', max_tokens: 120 });
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat', payload, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED' } });
  sleep(Math.random()*0.18);
}
```

ops-bot: deploy job started (RB-7102) by nina at 1714506810

nina: quick follow-up (1714506834) after primed run (20m focused on bursts):
- chat p95 reduced to 355ms (very close to target)
- chat p50=195ms
- embeddings p95 unchanged ~145ms
- burst drop rate reduced to 0.7% (was 3.1%)
- two tail traces remain at ~1.5s but very rare
- incremental burst buffer cost estimate: +$1.2k/mo (reserved pool delta)

sophie: 355ms p95 is within negotiation range. we'll offer priming + burst buffer as recommended baseline and note runtime tuning as an optional engagement (estimated $4.5k retainer).

cal: please upload CSV + flame graphs to the deal folder and add the config blob to the proposal. Also draft 2-3 lines about encryption/KMS for the security questionnaire (Helios asked about Dedicated KMS support).

nina: uploaded report: https://drive.redwood.example/heliosmetrics/perf/1714506789-report.zip contains CSV, flame graphs, and run configs. Drafting the KMS blurb now: 
- Dedicated: envelope encryption with customer KMS integration available on request; audit logs export to customer SIEM.

mike-eng: closing notes: if Helios insists on strict <350ms p95 for all traffic, we recommend the eng-runtime tuning path after baseline deployment. Otherwise priming + burst buffer should be the default and keeps engineering effort minimal.

cal: thanks team. I'll update pricing sheet with +$1.2k/mo and add optional $4.5k tuning line. dropping this into the SOW draft.

nina: will monitor and re-open if eng-runtime needs to be involved. :white_check_mark:
